entries.title: Trustees of the Rural Private Hospital Association of Kenya v Chief Executive Officer, National Hospital Insurance Fund & 2 Others
entries.principle: Locus standi in constitutional petitions is broad; associations may sue in the interest of their members under Article 258.
entries.facts: An association of private hospitals challenged the actions of the NHIF. The petitioners alleged violations of constitutional rights. The case raised questions of standing and association suits.
entries.holding: The Court held that locus standi in constitutional petitions is broad under Article 258; associations may sue in the interest of their members.

entries.title: Council of Governors v Senate & 2 Others
entries.principle: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is confined to matters concerning county government; the Senate's oversight role over county revenue is constitutionally entrenched.
entries.facts: A reference by the Council of Governors on the division of revenue between national and county governments.
entries.holding: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is confined to matters concerning county government; the Senate's oversight role over county revenue is constitutionally entrenched.
entries.judges: Maraga CJ, Mwilu DCJ, Ibrahim, Wanjala, Ndung'u and Lenaola SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: Legal Consequences of the Separation of the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius in 1965 (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: The process of decolonisation must respect the right to self-determination; a detachment agreed by the administering power without the consent of the people is unlawful.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the legal consequences of the separation of the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius.
entries.holding: The process of decolonisation must respect the right to self-determination; a detachment agreed by the administering power without the consent of the people is unlawful.

entries.title: Thuranira Salesio Mutuma & Another v County Government of Meru & Another
entries.principle: Locus standi in constitutional petitions is broad; any person may institute proceedings claiming a contravention of the Constitution, including in the public interest.
entries.facts: A petition challenging the actions of the County Government of Meru. The petitioners alleged violations of constitutional rights. The case raised questions of standing and public interest litigation.
entries.holding: The Court held that locus standi in constitutional petitions is broad under Article 258; any person may institute proceedings claiming a contravention of the Constitution, including in the public interest.

entries.title: Speaker of the Senate v Speaker of the National Assembly & 4 Others
entries.principle: Bicameralism requires that both Houses of Parliament participate in the legislative process; a Bill concerning counties must be considered by the Senate.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the role of the Senate in the legislative process.
entries.holding: Bicameralism requires that both Houses of Parliament participate in the legislative process; a Bill concerning counties must be considered by the Senate.
entries.judges: Mutunga CJ, Tunoi, Ibrahim, Ojwang, Wanjala and Ndung'u SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Saif Al-Islam Gaddafi and Abdullah Al-Senussi
entries.citation: ICC-01/11-01/11, Pre-Trial Chamber I, Decision on the admissibility challenge (31 May 2013)
entries.principle: A case is inadmissible where the accused has already been tried for substantially the same conduct, unless the national proceedings lacked independence or impartiality or were designed to shield the accused.
entries.facts: Saif Al-Islam Gaddafi and Abdullah Al-Senussi were charged with crimes against humanity during the Libyan revolution.
entries.holding: A case is inadmissible where the accused has already been tried for substantially the same conduct, unless the national proceedings lacked independence or impartiality or were designed to shield the accused.

entries.title: Jurisdictional Immunities of the State (Germany v Italy: Greece intervening)
entries.principle: State immunity is a rule of customary international law; the territorial tort exception does not apply to acts of the armed forces in the conduct of armed conflict.
entries.facts: Germany claimed that Italy violated its immunity by allowing civil claims for war crimes.
entries.holding: State immunity is a rule of customary international law; the territorial tort exception does not apply to acts of the armed forces in the conduct of armed conflict.

entries.title: Okiya Omtatah Okoiti v Attorney General
entries.principle: A constitutional petition must be brought by a person with sufficient interest; public interest litigation is permitted where the matter is of general public importance.
entries.facts: Okiya Omtatah Okoiti petitioned the High Court challenging government action. The petitioner sought to enforce constitutional rights. The case raised questions of standing and public interest litigation.
entries.holding: A constitutional petition must be brought by a person with sufficient interest; public interest litigation is permitted where the matter is of general public importance.

entries.title: Samuel Kamau Macharia & Another v Kenya Commercial Bank Limited & 2 Others
entries.principle: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of its jurisdiction at the threshold; a decision reached without jurisdiction is a nullity. Jurisdiction flows from the Constitution or statute, not from consent or convenience.
entries.facts: An application challenging the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in a dispute between Samuel Kamau Macharia and Kenya Commercial Bank. The applicant sought to invoke the Court\
entries.holding: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of its jurisdiction at the threshold; jurisdiction flows from the Constitution or statute, not from consent or convenience.
entries.judges: Mutunga CJ, Tunoi, Ibrahim, Ojwang, Wanjala and Ndung'u SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: In the Matter of the Interim Independent Electoral Commission
entries.principle: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is a special jurisdiction, exercisable only within Article 163(6) and confined to matters of public importance concerning devolved government; it is not a general consultative power.
entries.facts: The Interim Independent Electoral Commission sought an advisory opinion from the Supreme Court on the conduct of by-elections following the 2010 Constitution. The reference raised questions of devolution, electoral management and the scope of the Court\
entries.holding: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is a special jurisdiction, exercisable only within Article 163(6) and confined to matters of public importance concerning devolved government.
entries.judges: Mutunga CJ, Tunoi, Ibrahim, Ojwang, Wanjala and Ndung'u SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: Accordance with International Law of the Unilateral Declaration of Independence in respect of Kosovo (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: General international law does not prohibit declarations of independence; the legality of a declaration depends on the particular circumstances of each case.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the legality of Kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence.
entries.holding: General international law does not prohibit declarations of independence; the legality of a declaration depends on the particular circumstances of each case.

entries.title: James Katabazi and 21 Others v Secretary General of the East African Community and Another
entries.principle: The Court will not abdicate its jurisdiction to interpret the Treaty merely because the dispute touches on human rights; the simple answer to whether it has jurisdiction over human-rights violations is no, but it will still interpret the Treaty.
entries.facts: James Katabazi and 21 others challenged their detention by the Ugandan government before the EACJ.
entries.holding: The Court will not abdicate its jurisdiction to interpret the Treaty merely because the dispute touches on human rights; the simple answer to whether it has jurisdiction over human-rights violations is no, but it will still interpret the Treaty.

entries.title: Arrest Warrant of 11 April 2000 (Democratic Republic of the Congo v Belgium)
entries.principle: An incumbent Minister for Foreign Affairs enjoys absolute immunity from criminal jurisdiction in foreign States, even for alleged war crimes or crimes against humanity.
entries.facts: The DRC challenged Belgium's issuance of an arrest warrant for its Minister for Foreign Affairs.
entries.holding: An incumbent Minister for Foreign Affairs enjoys absolute immunity from criminal jurisdiction in foreign States, even for alleged war crimes or crimes against humanity.

entries.title: Speaker of the National Assembly v Samuel Kamau Macharia
entries.principle: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of its jurisdiction at the threshold; a decision reached without jurisdiction is a nullity.
entries.facts: A dispute between the Speaker of the National Assembly and Samuel Kamau Macharia over parliamentary privilege.
entries.holding: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of its jurisdiction at the threshold; a decision reached without jurisdiction is a nullity.
entries.judges: Gicheru CJ, Kwach and Cockar JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Duško Tadić
entries.court: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia
entries.principle: An armed conflict exists whenever there is protracted armed violence between governmental authorities and organised armed groups or between such groups within a State.

entries.title: Speaker of the National Assembly v Karume
entries.principle: Where the Constitution prescribes a specific procedure or forum, that procedure must be followed; the court will not permit a party to achieve indirectly, through a different route, what the Constitution requires to be done another way.
entries.facts: The Speaker of the National Assembly challenged a High Court order that had restrained Parliament from debating a motion. The dispute arose in the context of the transition from the former Constitution to the 2010 Constitution. The Court of Appeal was asked to determine whether the High Court had properly exercised its jurisdiction.
entries.holding: Where the Constitution prescribes a specific procedure or forum, that procedure must be followed; courts will not imply a different route to circumvent the constitutional text.
entries.judges: Gachuhi, Cockar and Omolo JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: Western Sahara (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: The principle of self-determination applies to all non-self-governing territories; historical ties do not affect the application of the principle.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the status of Western Sahara.
entries.holding: The principle of self-determination applies to all non-self-governing territories; historical ties do not affect the application of the principle.

entries.title: Legal Consequences for States of the Continued Presence of South Africa in Namibia (Advisory Opinion)
entries.principle: The continued presence of a mandatory power after the termination of the mandate is illegal; States are under a duty not to recognise the illegal situation.
entries.facts: An advisory opinion on the legal consequences of South Africa's continued presence in Namibia.
entries.holding: The continued presence of a mandatory power after the termination of the mandate is illegal; States are under a duty not to recognise the illegal situation.

entries.title: Barcelona Traction, Light and Power Company, Limited (Belgium v Spain)
entries.principle: Obligations erga omnes are owed to the international community as a whole; the right to protect them is not confined to the State directly injured.
entries.facts: Belgium claimed on behalf of Belgian shareholders of a Canadian company expropriated by Spain.
entries.holding: Obligations erga omnes are owed to the international community as a whole; the right to protect them is not confined to the State directly injured.

entries.title: Monetary Gold Removed from Rome in 1943 (Italy v France, United Kingdom and United States)
entries.principle: The Court cannot exercise jurisdiction where the legal interests of an absent third State form the very subject matter of the decision (the indispensable-party principle).
entries.facts: Italy claimed reparation for gold removed from Rome during World War II.
entries.holding: The Court cannot exercise jurisdiction where the legal interests of an absent third State form the very subject matter of the decision (the indispensable-party principle).

entries.title: Charter of the United Nations
entries.citation: Charter of the United Nations (adopted 26 June 1945, entered into force 24 October 1945) 1 UNTS XVI
entries.principle: Member States must settle disputes peacefully and perform Charter obligations in good faith; Charter obligations prevail over conflicting treaty commitments.

entries.title: Statute of the International Court of Justice
entries.citation: Statute of the International Court of Justice (1945) 33 UNTS 993
entries.principle: The Court's jurisdiction depends on the consent of States; Article 38(1) enumerates the sources it applies; Article 59 confines a decision's binding force to the parties and to that case.

entries.title: S.S. Lotus (France v Turkey)
entries.principle: Restrictions on the exercise of jurisdiction are exceptional: a State is free to exercise jurisdiction unless a permissive rule of international law prohibits it, and State sovereignty is the default.
entries.facts: A collision between a French and a Turkish vessel on the high seas; France challenged Turkey's jurisdiction to try the Turkish officer.
entries.holding: Restrictions on the exercise of jurisdiction are exceptional: a State is free to exercise jurisdiction unless a permissive rule of international law prohibits it.
entries.judges: Huber, President (Permanent Court of International Justice)
entries.note: Often invoked against expansive jurisdictional claims; distinguish where sovereignty arguments are being made.
